description: Scenario presets for the volume flood view (FLOOD_MODEL_PLAN.md section 4.6, Phase V). Every total is an estimate chosen to illustrate a mechanism, not a measured event. Levels are ODN metres; the surge is the rise of high water above ordinary high water (Trinity High Water, os-tide-levels.json).

riverLevelODN.note: Held level on the non-tidal water (the Lea above the locks, the upper Channelsea and the other reaches outside the tide polygons). The default is the model's retained datum, 0.06 m scene (tide_levels.RETAINED). Phase 2 replaces this with pound levels from the Lea flow.

presets.label: Ordinary day
presets.caption: No rain, an ordinary tide and the river at its usual level.

presets.label: Summer storms, 1888 (estimate)
presets.caption: A thunderstorm and two more downpours over three days, with ordinary tides. The total, 50 mm, is an estimate: the report gives no rainfall figure.
presets.evidence: historic-flood-events.json 1888-07-30-rainfall-sequence (trove-107325485): rainfall and local drainage flooding on Hackney Marshes, around Temple Mills and in Plaistow; no river peak or surge established. No measured total found (search, 6 October 2026).

presets.label: Winter storm, high tides (estimate)
presets.caption: 40 mm of rain in a day while high water stands 0.4 m above ordinary: the sluices drain for less of each tide.
presets.evidence: Illustrative. The surge is a modest spring-tide-plus-wind rise, well below the 1928 peak.

presets.label: Surge to the 1928 height (one tide)
presets.caption: High water about 5.1 m ODN, the 1928 peak near Bow, on the 1890s ground for one tide. The 1928 walls and ground were not those of the 1890s.
presets.evidence: lea-control-structures.json navigationNormalHead method: 1928-01-07 peak at Bow about 5.1 m ODN (digitisedGaugePeaks1928); ordinary high water 3.41 m ODN.

presets.label: River held high for a day (estimate)
presets.caption: The non-tidal reaches held at 3.4 m ODN for a day with 20 mm of rain. The level is an estimate until Phase 2 computes the pounds from the Lea flow.
presets.evidence: Illustrative; the 1894 G2G peak at Feildes Weir (40.9 m³/s daily mean) has no level yet.
